content: Healthcare providers are advised to use a communication style that focuses on the individual patient, is culturally appropriate, and emphasizes the patient’s strengths. This involves actively listening to the patient, respecting their personal preferences and beliefs, and considering their levels of health literacy and numeracy. The goal of this approach is to improve both the patient’s health outcomes and their overall quality of life. By adopting this method, healthcare providers can more effectively understand and meet the unique needs and expectations of each patient, which is especially critical in the management of chronic conditions such as diabetes. (Grade B) Patients with diabetes can benefit significantly from care provided by a well-coordinated, interprofessional healthcare team. This team may include professionals such as diabetes care and education specialists, nurses, registered dietitian nutritionists, exercise specialists, pharmacists, dentists, podiatrists, and behavioral health professionals. (Grade E)
